getStarted.title: Get started
getStarted.intro: BioResearcher is an Agent Skills package: any harness that reads SKILL.md can load it. Pick your channel below — the biomedical MCP server (biomcp) is required for the research skills and can be bootstrapped automatically by the onboarding skill.
requirements: uv + python3 — the plotting and weekly-parsing skills bootstrap their own Python dependencies

channels.name: A · skills CLI (any harness)
channels.desc: Works with opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and every SKILL.md reader. Add just the onboarding skill to bootstrap the MCP runtime automatically.
channels.code:
npx skills add yeyuan98/bioresearcher-skills
# bootstrap the runtime immediately:
npx skills add yeyuan98/bioresearcher-skills --skill bioresearcher-onboard

channels.name: B · Claude Code plugin marketplace
channels.desc: Bundles the pinned biomcp MCP server (auto-starts, no manual .mcp.json) plus the deep-research worker subagent.

channels.name: C · WorkBuddy connector market
channels.desc: One market install: MCP server (npmmirror registry, managed Node 22) + four skills with Chinese/English descriptions. Search for “BioResearcher 生物医学研究”.
channels.code: # WorkBuddy -> connector market -> BioResearcher 生物医学研究 -> install

channels.name: D · git clone
channels.desc: Clone into the skills directory your harness reads (.opencode/skills/, .claude/skills/, .agents/skills/, .codex/skills/, .gemini/skills/).

getStarted.chinaBody: The onboarding skill auto-detects network conditions and switches to the npmmirror registry for Node and biomcp downloads; the uv skill supports China PyPI mirrors; the WorkBuddy connector uses npmmirror by default. Upstream biomedical APIs (NCBI, ClinicalTrials.gov, MyGene…) are global endpoints — set HTTP(S)_PROXY on restricted networks.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.intro: The questions partners and users ask most. Each answer links the full documentation.

items.a: Skills are authored in English (ecosystem convention for stable cross-harness triggering); the agent replies in the prompt's language — a Chinese prompt yields a Chinese report, with a true-run demo as proof. The WorkBuddy connector ships official zh descriptions and example prompts.
No — every demo on this site ran keyless. The only exceptions: OncoKB annotations require a token, and DisGeNET falls back to OpenTargets without one. Keys raise rate limits (e.g. NCBI 3→10 req/s).

items.q: Does it work from mainland China?
items.a: Yes — onboarding/uv skills and the WorkBuddy connector use npmmirror/China mirrors automatically; upstream biomedical APIs may need a proxy (HTTP(S)_PROXY is honored).

items.q: Why do the demo reports open directly here, when GitHub can't render them?
items.a: Because this site embeds the byte-exact final_report.html committed in the repository — the same file whose provenance is pinned by the repo commit. Nothing is re-rendered for display.

No — and not merely by instruction. Since deep-research 1.5+ the citation pipeline is key-based end-to-end: workers append every citable source to an evidence ledger, the draft is authored with [@pmid:...] cite-key markers, and the render script is the single numbering authority (it hard-fails on any key without a ledger record); an independent auditor then re-checks the rendered report (contiguous [1]..[N], NCBI cross-check). Hand-assembled bibliographies are structurally impossible.

items.q: How many tokens / how long do runs take?
items.a: Measured (opencode 1.18.30, deep-research 1.7.0 with parallel dispatch): interview 33 s; PubMed parse 56 s; deep research EN 545 s / ZH 649 s; structural figure incl. dependency install 1064 s. The MCP probes are token-free.
All queries hit public biomedical APIs only; reports and figures stay local to your project; the repo contains no telemetry; demo artifacts contain no credentials.
Apache-2.0 (repo LICENSE and the upstream biomcp-ts project). Commercial use and derivatives permitted with the license notice retained; citation metadata in CITATION.cff.

items.q: Does it work in Cursor / Codex / WorkBuddy?
items.a: Yes — any harness that reads SKILL.md and can run an MCP server. See the compatibility matrix in the agent doc §4.5.

items.q: How do I reproduce the demos?
items.a: Clone the repo and run node demos/run-demo.mjs --list; replay any case with --only <id> --publish. Agent cases spend LLM tokens (manual-run only); the MCP probes are token-free.

mcp.title: The MCP server: biomcp-ts
mcp.intro: biomcp-ts (npm package biomcp, pinned 1.4.0) is an MCP server for biomedical data: 41 core + 15 optional tools over stdio JSON-RPC, spanning articles, trials, genes, variants, drugs, diseases, patents, omics databases, GTEx and Ensembl/PDB — keyless by default, rate-limited in-process.
mcp.wiringBody: With the server named biomcp, tools surface as biomcp_article_search, biomcp_gene_get, … Exact version pinning via -p is mandatory (bare npx biomcp cannot resolve peer deps).
mcp.wiringMore: Full wiring matrix (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …)
mcp.capturesIntro: Real request/response pairs captured by a deterministic stdio probe — not hand-written examples.

demos.title: Demo cases

Every case carries objective checks, curated transcripts and commit-pinned artifacts in the repository.
